name: Museum Arnhem
funding: Run by Stichting Musea Arnhem since 2014 on an annual Gemeente Arnhem subsidy (€2.6M in 2011).

name: Van Doesburg-Rinsemahuis
funding: Museum Dr8888 runs it. In 2025 subsidy was EUR 884k of EUR 1.189M income. Subsidy from Smallingerland and the province of Fryslân is its essential base.

name: Van Abbemuseum
funding: Eindhoven municipality, Mondriaan Fund, Ammodo, Creative Europe and the Promotors foundation; VriendenLoterij, a public charity lottery, is also listed as a supporter.

name: Van Schijndel House
funding: Not confirmed. The volunteer-run Mart van Schijndel Foundation (set up 2008) runs visits for a EUR 45 donation. The house is still privately lived in and no owner is named.

name: Kunstfort bij Vijfhuizen
funding: The Mondriaan Fonds granted 225.000 euros for Kunstpodium Basis 2025-2028 to Stichting Kunstfort Activiteiten, Vijfhuizen.

name: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
funding: Run by Tātaki Auckland Unlimited for Auckland Council. Partners include BMW, Van Cleef & Arpels, HSBC, Anthony Harper and Baker Tilly. Trusts include Chartwell and Mackelvie.

name: Christchurch Art Gallery
funding: Christchurch City Council; the Christchurch Art Gallery Foundation raises acquisition funds. Partners are JBWere (foundation partner) and Anthony Harper (major partner), plus hotel, design and drinks suppliers.

name: Dunedin Public Art Gallery
funding: Dunedin City Council gallery. Gallery Partners are Creative New Zealand, Quartz Reef and Craigs Investment Partners; the DPAG Society buys works.

name: The Dowse Art Museum
funding: Mostly funded by Hutt City Council, plus the Dowse Foundation; Jan 2025 archive names Dulux as a corporate partner and Steel & Tube as a donor.

name: Sarjeant Gallery
funding: Whanganui District Council ($26.1M) led the NZ$79.4M rebuild with the Ministry for Culture and Heritage, Lottery Grants Board, Provincial Growth Fund, Stout Trust and other unnamed trusts.

name: Fundación Casa de los Tres Mundos
funding: Small cultural foundation built with German, Austrian, Swiss and Dutch government grants and the City of Granada; closed by the Nicaraguan state in 2024.
